The reviewed capability state of the product, and every sentence on the site that mentions an org. tests/honesty.spec.cjs refuses any claim sentence not listed here, on any surface. Deny by default: new copy in the risk class fails until a person reads it against `capability` below. Seeded 2026-09-09 from the site as it then stood, after reading all of it - so its value is PROSPECTIVE, not a retrospective blessing.
_asserts: Each claim names the capability it would imply if read as a present-tense statement, or `none` for positioning and denials. A claim may not assert a capability that is false. That is what makes `capability` load-bearing rather than decorative.
_capability_note: The last two are deliberately separate and the distinction is load-bearing. A person doing a read-only review inside a paid engagement needs no connector; the automated path that reads an org and returns a grade does not exist. The homepage relies on that distinction without stating it - see OPEN QUESTION below.
_open_question: TWO sentences on index.html lean on a distinction the page never states, and the gate below surfaced both rather than letting them through. (1) The hero deck: 'We measure what an enterprise Salesforce org is quietly costing... put a number on it, and say what to fix first.' (2) 'A read-only look at the org fills in the rest.' Both sit near 'What does not exist yet is the part that reads a live org' and 'Nothing here has scored anyone's Salesforce instance.' All four are true under the capability split above - the first two describe what a person does in a paid engagement, the last two describe the automated connector - but a visitor is given no way to see they are about different things. That is a copy decision for Mr. Salam, not one for me to settle quietly in a test fixture. Recorded here, and raised with him.
